package_info.package_manager: source (C++ library, used in OpenSAML/Shibboleth, distributed via Linux repos and bundled in proprietary products)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2023-36661) that allows attackers to supply malicious XML input, causing the library to resolve attacker-controlled URIs via the <RetrievalMethod> element in KeyInfo. This can be exploited to access internal resources, exfiltrate sensitive data, cause denial of service, or be chained with other vulnerabilities for unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability is present by default in affected versions and can be triggered without authentication or user interaction.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the application processes SAML/XML input containing a KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod element.
execution_context.file_location: Core xmltooling library (C++), typically invoked by applications using OpenSAML or Shibboleth (e.g., shibd process).
required_permissions: filesystem (to write/read temporary files if external resources are stored locally)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This XML snippet, when processed by the vulnerable xmltooling library, causes the application to fetch and process the external URI specified in the RetrievalMethod element. The library does not restrict the URI scheme or destination, allowing an attacker to trigger arbitrary outbound network requests (SSRF) to internal or external resources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows untrusted XML input to specify arbitrary external URIs, which the application will fetch and process without validation. This enables attackers to force the application to make network requests to attacker-controlled or internal resources, potentially exposing sensitive data, enabling lateral movement, or facilitating further exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure SAML/XML libraries are expected to restrict or validate external resource loading, especially from untrusted input, to prevent SSRF and related attacks. The vulnerable behavior allows arbitrary URI resolution from untrusted XML, violating secure parsing and resource resolution best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate SAML implementations may use RetrievalMethod to fetch keys from trusted, pre-configured, and whitelisted locations. However, they should never allow arbitrary URIs from untrusted or user-supplied XML input, and should enforce strict validation of allowed URI schemes and destinations.
key_indicators: Unrestricted resolution of external URIs from KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements in XML input
Absence of URI scheme or destination validation in XML parsing logic
Outbound network requests initiated by SAML/XML parsing routines in shibd or similar processes
Ability to specify arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS URIs in SAML/XML input that are fetched by the application

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits malicious SAML/XML input containing a KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod element with an attacker-controlled URI.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable xmltooling library processes the XML and fetches the external URI, resulting in SSRF.

attack_chain.action: The SSRF is used to access internal resources or trigger further vulnerabilities (e.g., chaining with command injection for RCE).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential unauthenticated remote code execution, data exfiltration, or denial of service.

behavioral_signatures: Parsing of SAML/XML input triggers outbound network requests to untrusted or unexpected destinations
Presence of KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements with external URIs in SAML/XML input
shibd or similar SAML-processing processes making HTTP/HTTPS requests during XML parsing
Unexpected network activity correlated with XML parsing events
file_indicators: SAML/XML files containing <RetrievalMethod URI="http://..."> or <RetrievalMethod URI="https://..."> elements
SAML/XML input with RetrievalMethod elements referencing non-whitelisted or external domains
Unexpected or unlogged network activity from shibd or SAML-processing services during XML parsing
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled or non-whitelisted domains from SAML-processing hosts
Requests to internal resources (e.g., 169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata) triggered by SAML/XML parsing
Network connections initiated by shibd or similar processes to destinations specified in SAML/XML input
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SAML/XML parsing services (such as shibd) for outbound network requests during XML processing, especially those initiated by parsing KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements. Flag any SAML/XML input containing external URIs or unexpected URI schemes in RetrievalMethod. Use network monitoring to detect requests to untrusted or internal destinations originating from SAML-processing applications. Correlate network activity with XML parsing events. Patch xmltooling to v3.2.4+ or apply the BlockingXSECURIResolver fix to prevent exploitation.
